newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products fall, gas oil premiums shrink.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products fall, gas oil premiums shrink.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products declined on Thursday, with gas oil premiums under pressure from increasing supply, traders said.
Gas oil slid on weaker IPE futures and premiums were under pressure from increased supply in thin trade.
"People want to wait to see where prices are going before committing themselves," one trader said.

A cargo of Russian was reported done at Nov IPE flat cif Genoa for delivery in seven days, but traders said the vessel was of poor quality and some said the deal was believed designed specifically to push the market lower.
Naphtha prices fell slightly as traders said there was little demand ahead of November programmes.
"I'm not seeing much end-user demand in the Med or in northwest Europe," said one trader.
A full range Egyptian cargo was still believed on offer in the Med but no trades were confirmed.
Gasoline prices were sharply lower but recovered slightly with a rebound in Brent crude and NYMEX gasoline futures, traders said. Premium unleaded was priced at $225/$229 fob, down $7 from Wednesday.
Fuel oil activity was broadly limited to paper trading because most players were steering clear of physical trades in the current falling market.

"Buyers are only interested in floating prices. There's a feeling the market still has room to fall," said one Med trader. The high sulphur cracked sector also came under pressure by at least one trader offering aggressively low in order to secure a cheaper price on a much larger cargo. Prices were pegged as low as $110-112 fob Med.
The low sulphur market was frusted by continued congestion in Milazzo, seemingly knocking out the main buyer. --London newsroom +44 542 171 7646
